subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Left shoulder pain for three weeks
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: Hi, I'm Wayne. I'm not sure about my exact age, but I'm in my late 40s. I'm here because I've been having this left shoulder pain for about three weeks now. It's been pretty constant and it really hurts when I try to lift things or even lay on that shoulder at night. Doctor: Could you please confirm your exact age and gender, and describe the nature of the left shoulder pain in more detail, such as whether it is sharp, dull, or throbbing, and if there are any associated symptoms like numbness or weakness? Patient: I'm not sure about my exact age, but I'm in my late 40s, and I'm male. The pain is more of a constant ache, but it gets sharper when I try to move my arm or put pressure on it. It doesn't feel numb or weak, just really sore, especially at night when I try to lay on that shoulder. Doctor: Have you experienced any trauma or injury to your left shoulder in the past three weeks? Additionally, have you had any previous shoulder issues or surgeries? Patient: I don't remember any specific injury to my shoulder, but I have been doing a lot of work in my basement lately, so maybe I did something while doing that. I have had some aches and pains before, but nothing serious—just stuff that Tylenol could handle. Doctor: Have you experienced any swelling, redness, or warmth in the left shoulder area? Have you noticed any limitation in the range of motion of your left arm? Patient: Yes, I have noticed a limitation in the range of motion of my left arm. It hurts when I try to reach for something or lift objects, and I don’t even try to reach over my head because it really hurts. It feels like my shoulder is just not moving the way it should. Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies or consultations with a healthcare provider
